summary: [Regression] AEM Guides 2026.3.0 – Editor UI no longer shows XML/DITA tags (tagsView ignored)
description:
*Customer Context*

• Customer / IMS Org ID: 945D02BE532957400A490D4C@AdobeOrg (Red Hat)  
• Program & Environment: cm-p63456-e531328 (Stage) & local SDKs running 2026.3.0.337  
• Current (broken) build: AEM Guides 2026.3.0.337  
• Last known good build: AEM Guides 2026.1.0.324 (Prod)  
• Product entitlement in SFDC: AEM On-Premise (dx\_aem\_onprem) – but issue reproduced on Cloud (Stage) after upgrade to 2026.3.0.337  
 

*Business Impact (Large / P2)*

Authors can no longer see XML/DITA tags inside the Web Editor. • Structured-authoring workflow disrupted – writers cannot identify elements and must switch to “Tags On” manually for every session and file.  
• ~40 technical writers blocked from efficient authoring, risking delays to documentation delivery tied to upcoming product releases.  
• Issue impacts all Stage users and local developer instances; Production (still on 2026.1) works, so go-live upgrade is on hold.  
 

*Issue Details*

Since upgrading Stage to AEM Guides 2026.3.0.337 the XML Web Editor opens with {{Tags Off}}. • Adding {{tagsView}}:{{true}} in {{ui_config.json}} no longer forces _Tags On_ for new sessions.  
• Every new browser session defaults to _Tags Off_, regardless of the setting.  
• Manually enabling tags via Menu → Show → Tags works, but the preference is not retained.  
• Same behaviour reproduced on un-customised local Cloud SDK (2026.3.0.337).  
• Production running 2026.1.0.324 shows tags by default, honouring the exact same {{ui_config.json}} snippet.  
 

*Steps to Reproduce (2026.3.0.337)*

• Open {{https://author-p63456-e531328.adobeaemcloud.com/libs/fmdita/clientlibs/xmleditor/page.html?...}}  
• Load any DITA topic.  
• Observe that element tags and metadata tags are missing (Tags overlay off).  
• Open {{Menu → Show → Tags}}; tags appear.  
• Close Editor and reopen – tags are off again.  
 

*Expected Result*

When {{defaultValues.tagsView=true}} is present in {{ui_config.json}} (see official docs – [Configure default value for Tags View|https://experienceleague.adobe.com/docs/experience-manager-guides/using/install-guide/cs-ig/web-editor-configs-cs/configure-default-value-tags-view.html]), the Web Editor should launch with Tags View enabled for all new sessions (as in 2026.1). User can still toggle it off manually.

*Actual Result*

Tags View is always disabled on initial load; setting in {{ui_config.json}} is ignored. User must enable tags each time.

*Relevant Configuration Snippet*

{code}
{
  "defaultValues": {
    "tagsView": true,
    "largeFileTagCount": 2500
  }
}
{code}

*Support Investigation Summary*

• Verified same {{ui_config.json}} works on Prod (2026.1) – tags show by default.  
• Reproduced on Stage and clean local SDK with 2026.3.0.337 – tags hidden.  
• No console errors; no relevant server-side stack traces.  
• Confirmed with doc ([link|https://experienceleague.adobe.com/docs/experience-manager-guides/using/install-guide/cs-ig/web-editor-configs-cs/configure-default-value-tags-view.html]) that {{tagsView}} is still the correct key.  
• Checked release notes/fixed-issues for 2026.3 – no mention of change to Tags View default.  
• Suspected regression; not covered by known issues. Requested escalation (see Case E-002152522).  
 

*Attachments / Evidence*

• Video & screenshots demonstrating missing tags (see Dynamics case E-002152522).  
• Stage url with issue: {{https://author-p63456-e531328.adobeaemcloud.com/.../test-task.dita}}  
 

*Request / Next Steps*

• Engineering triage to confirm regression in 2026.3.0 branch.   
• Identify root cause: why {{defaultValues.tagsView}} ignored / user preference not persisted.  
• Provide hotfix or confirm target patch / release where behaviour is restored.  
• Advise if any interim OSGi or UI configuration override can re-enable Tags View by default.  
 

*Priority / Severity*

P2 – Urgent (large user impact, production upgrade blocked).

Full investigation available here: https://aemcs-workspace.adobe.com/bot/dynamics/investigation/ea6d29ee-02d4-4024-a2d6-65d2171a746c

*Problem statement and scenario :*

 

Let's suppose Enterprise wants to translate  "topic 1. dita " from "en " to " de" for the first time.

 
 # Enterprise sends two versions of the same topic for translation, starting with version 1.1 and then version 1.2.
 # *Translation copy :*
 ** AEM Guides creates a working copy of version 1.1 in German (i.e., {{{}/content/dam/de/topic.dita{}}}).
 ** For version 1.2, a temporary copy is created in the output folder (i.e., {{{}/content/dam/projects/translation_output/xxxx.dita{}}}).
 # I{*}mport/Aprroval order{*} :
 ** If version 1.2 translation is exported and approved before version 1.1, the German working copy ({{{}/content/dam/de/topic.dita{}}}) gets updated with version 1.2 content.
 # {*}Incorrect translation export{*}:
 ** When the version 1.1 translation is later exported, it will point to the updated German working copy (version 1.2), causing an inconsistency.

{*}Impact{*}: This leads to an incorrect translation for version 1.1, which may go unnoticed until the customer realizes the discrepancy, potentially causing delays or errors in the translation and publication process.

 

*Workaround :*

Send translation for version 1.1 again or shift back to legacy translation.

*Potential Solutions :*
 * Introduce a workflow that ensures translations for different version are reviewed independently before updating the working copy in the DAM.

h3. Issue Summary

After upgrading the TD-2 environment to Guides 4.6 UUID and AEM 6.5.21, Native PDF generation fails for content using the `@chunk="to-content"` attribute. This issue does not occur in the TD-1 environment, which runs Guides 4.1.3.5 and AEM 6.5.18-SSP1. Screenshots of successful and failed PDF generations, along with the source DITA XML, are provided by the customer.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

*   Upload the topics to a folder in Assets.
*   Open the map in the Advanced Map editor.
*   Generate a Native PDF.
*   Observe that text in the topic files is not present in the Native PDF.

h3. Expected Behavior

The content should generate correctly in the Native PDF, including the text from the topic files.

h3. Actual Behavior

Text in the topic files is missing from the generated Native PDF in the upgraded environment.

h3. Support Investigation

Support has set up a test instance with SP21 and Guides 4.6 UUID. We are able to replicate the issue somewhat but not to the extent of the customers report. There is no problem with PDF generation in our tests, the PDFs generate but the expected elements and format are not correct. The child topic, and the grandchildren topics, are entirely missing when 'chunk' is used . Support seeks further clarification on replicating the failure in the TD-2 environment.  
Have a test package created and attached to replicate the test.   
\- Install Content Package: broadcom-chunk-test-2.0.zip  
\- Navigate to the 2 Map files marked “chunk test” and generate them each with Sites output and with Native PDF output and see the differences between them  
\- Also navigate to the 2 Mapfiles marked “No Chunk test” to see the behavior when Chunking is not included.   
(Tested outputs attached as well)
This example package is based on the DITA-OT example map from https://www.oxygenxml.com/dita/1.3/specs/archSpec/base/chunkingexamples.html, example #3. In example 3 it states
{quote}The following map will generate two chunks: parent1.xxxx will contain only topic P1, while child1.xxxx will contain topic C1, with topics GC1 and GC2 nested within C1{quote} but the actual output contains only topic P1.

h3. Relevant JIRA Insights

According to JIRA ticket GUIDES-19698, there was a regression in Guides 4.6 affecting heading levels in Native PDFs, which might relate to the chunking issue. This was resolved by allowing heading levels beyond H6 to be correctly created.

*   Verify that all configurations from the older environment are correctly migrated to the new setup.
*   Check that the latest patches addressing Native PDF generation in Guides 4.6 are applied.
*   Conduct comprehensive testing with varied content structures to ensure resolved JIRA issues have addressed the chunking problems.

h3. Customer Impact

The issue affects the customer's ability to generate PDFs with the expected content using the upgraded system, potentially impacting document delivery or publishing processes.

description:
The following customer is using the Guides API to create a baseline as documented [here|https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-guides/using/api-reference/create-baseline-label-java]  and they are seeing a [500|https://splunk.or1.adobe.net/en-GB/app/TA-aem_skyline/search?earliest=1722936456.214&latest=1722936460.215&q=search%20(%60sky_edge_logs%60%20OR%20index%3D%22dx_aem_engineering%22)%20aem_service%3Dcm-p108407-e1173311%20aem_tier%3Dauthor%20%2Fbin%2FcreateBaselineApi&display.page.search.mode=smart&dispatch.sample_ratio=1&sid=1724267733.101375_75E8025B-8CA1-4E53-B9F1-31FCB54511E1] error when invoking the [BaslineUtils|https://git.corp.adobe.com/AdobeStarling/starling/blob/8eb192b4d334ea72f4edf1ea24d2bdf44c98c76b/core/api/src/main/java/com/adobe/fmdita/api/baselines/BaselineUtils.java#L90] service. 

 

The issue is because the [BundleActivator|https://git.corp.adobe.com/AdobeStarling/starling/blob/8eb192b4d334ea72f4edf1ea24d2bdf44c98c76b/core/api/src/main/java/com/adobe/fmdita/api/Activator.java#L21-L24] starts before the org.apache.sling.api.resource.ResourceResolverFactory can be referenced and because of that the BaselineUtils class throws a Guides exception. We were able to circumvent the issue by refreshing the Guides Baseline API bundle in order to retrigger the Bundle Activator but this cannot be done every time and can only be done by support since the customer does not have access to /system/console/bundles.

 

The correct solution is not to use a BundleActivator but instead use an @Reference annotated class variable in order to inject the org.apache.sling.api.resource.ResourceResolverFactory in the activator. This requires a refactor of the bundle, and remove the use of static functions to retrieve OSGi Declaritive Services. 

 

This issue is only visible in a true cloud instance because all the bundles start at the same time. In a local SDK you will not see this issue because you install the bundle after everything is started so the Activator find the org.apache.sling.api.resource.ResourceResolverFactory class successfully.

h3. Baseline Object Changes (v1 vs v2)

The baseline object in {*}v2 is fundamentally different from v1{*}.
 * In {*}v1{*}, the object contained several stale or mutable fields such as paths, labels, and versions, which could change over time in the system.

 * In {*}v2{*}, these have been removed. Only relevant and stable information is retained, represented in a graph-based structure.

 * Scope peer edge information is now included.

 * As a result, {*}v1 and v2 baseline objects are not compatible{*}.

h3. API and Object Exposure
 * In {*}v2{*}, there is {*}no API to fetch the raw baseline object{*}, as this object is an internal model. We dont want to api's to directly modify the baseline object

 * Users can retrieve *baseline references* and perform supported operations on them.

 * All values that were previously available through the _details API_ (used for reports and sanity checks) are still available.

 ** {{createBaseline}}

h3. Migration and Legacy Behavior
 * When baselines are migrated, {*}legacy baselines are not modified or deleted{*}.

 * They remain intact and are still available if the system is switched back to legacy mode.

 * Original state (legacy): {{{}baseline1{}}}, {{baseline2}}

h3. Async Migration Job

summary: Corrected the Handling of Alternate Text in AEM Guides to cater to DITA 1.2 standard
description:
h3. Issue Summary

Customer using AEM Guides 4.3.1 reports that alternate text for images is being added to the deprecated `@alt` attribute rather than the `<alt>` element, contrary to DITA 1.2 and 2.0 standards. A solution is required that complies with modern DITA standards and prepares for DITA 2.0 compatibility.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

1.  Check out a DITA topic and open it in the web editor.
2.  Click "Insert Image".
3.  Navigate to the image and click "Select".
4.  In the "Insert Image" window, type alternate text for the image in the "Alternate Text" field.
5.  Click "Insert".
6.  Click "Source" to view the markup and observe that the alternate text was added to the `@alt` attribute instead of the `<alt>` element.

h3. Expected Behavior

When an author inserts an image and specifies alternate text, the alternate text should be added within the `<alt>` element, following the DITA 1.2 standards, to ensure compatibility with DITA 2.0 and better practices.

h3. Actual Behavior

The alternate text is being incorrectly added to the `@alt` attribute of the image element in the AEM Guides, which is deprecated and not aligned with current standards.

h3. Investigation by Support

Support has acknowledged the issue and informed the customer that it has already been addressed in a newer version of AEM Guides. Support is seeking to confirm the version the customer is using to proceed accordingly. Customer has stated they are using AEM Guides version 4.3.1.

h3. Relevant JIRA Tickets

The investigation uncovered several JIRA tickets related to image handling and the `<alt>` element in AEM, with DXML-12568 being directly relevant to the issue at hand. The ticket discusses plans to update the Insert Image button behavior to comply with DITA standards.

h3. Next Steps

Engineering should refer to and act upon JIRA ticket DXML-12568 to ensure the Insert Image functionality adheres to DITA 2.0 standards. If the issue is not resolved in the latest patch, a hotfix or workaround should be provided. Customer communication should be maintained throughout the resolution process.

Full investigation available here: https://aemcs-workspace.adobe.com/bot/dynamics/investigation/44e16c7b-c9de-43f4-836b-30ff9692447b

Hi [~vinodgupta], I have investigated the issue and here's the analysis along with the numbers for the issue:

I have tried opening and editing the content.css file in the Hi-Tech template.

*{color:red}Before the fix{color}* with regards to the editing performance

For 

*{color:red}On-Prem:{color}*

*500 lines*:  it takes ~0.3s to load the 500 line css and type a character.
*1k lines*:  it takes ~0.5s to paste the 500 line css
*2k lines*:  it takes ~1.5s to paste 1k line css

*{color:red}On-Cloud:{color}*

*500 lines*:  it takes ~0.3s to load the 500 line css and type a character.
*1k lines*:  it takes ~0.5s to paste the 500 line css
*2k lines*:  it takes ~2s to paste 1k line css
*4k lines*:  it takes ~10s to paste 2k line css
*8k lines*:  application crashes and page is unresponsive.


With regards to *loading* of the document 

1. *~ 3k lines* : I am able to load the document but after a wait of 5s.
2. *~8k lines*: My application crashes and gets into an unresponsive state and I keep on waiting.

*{color:red}With the fix:{color}*

*{color:red}On prem numbers: {color}* 

1. loading happends in at most 1-2s with for a 100k line css document.
2. Typing is smooth in such a document every type I am getting a lag of only a few micro seconds.

*{color:red}Root Cause for the Issue: {color}*

Code editor is creating id cache everytime on every change in the document due to which there was a lag. What create id cache is doing internally is traversing through entire document and treating every document as if it's a xml document. So even in case of html/css file it's traversing and executing xml traversal functions, due to which the lag is coming on typing every character. This should ideally be enable for xml documents.

The customer is experiencing a bug within Guides 4.3.1.5, where tags included within a tag in topic titles are not being hidden in the Table of Contents (ToC) when generating a Native PDF.

The <draft-comment> within the <title> tag should be hidden in the ToC of the generated Native PDF, as well as other locations within the document  
  
*Actual Behavior*  
  
The <draft-comment> is visible in the ToC of the generated Native PDF, despite being expected to be hidden.

Support has validated the issue on a vanilla AEM instance with a TOC implemented. Related JIRA tickets DXML-10560 and DXML-11459 indicate that draft comments should be hidden by default in Native PDF templates, suggesting a possible regression or an incomplete fix. Another ticket, DXML-13622, while not directly related, discusses content structure and tagging in PDF output that may offer additional insights.  
  
*Action Taken*  
  
A DXML JIRA ticket will be created for the product team to review the bug and for the engineering team to investigate and address the issue.

summary: Issue with AEM Site Generation and Incremental Publish API
description:
h3. Customer and Incident Overview

The customer, Pooja Chauhan from EY (Ernst & Young), has reported an issue with Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) site generation. Specifically, the incremental site generation API is not reflecting the updated content on the AEM sites page when a ditamap includes localized content references.
h3. Relevant Investigation Findings

During the screen-sharing session, the support team was able to replicate the issue on an AEM 6.5 SP20 and AEM Guides version 4.4.0.40. The customer provided the steps to reproduce the issue, which involved setting up a local AEM instance, configuring DITA profiles, and inspecting ditamaps with localized content references. The Postman call made to trigger the Incremental Site generation API resulted in content not being generated, as observed in the AEM CRX/DE.
h3. Technical Details

The customer has provided technical details including:
 * AEM version: 6.5.18
 * FM Dita version: 4.3.0.347
 * Also reproducible on 6.5.20 and FM Dita 4.4.0.40 
 * ATLAS-6 QA Author environment URL and IP for reproducing the issue
 * Various documents and zip files with temp dita files
 * Error logs which may contain relevant information for troubleshooting

h3. Steps to Reproduce

1. With `mapref` attribute containing localization ditamap included in the base ditamap, and site generation triggered via incremental API with `fullMaps`.
2. Without `mapref` attribute, i.e., localization not included in the base ditamap, and site generation triggered via incremental API with `fullMaps`.
3. With `mapref` attribute containing localization ditamap included in the base ditamap, and site generation triggered via incremental API without `fullmap` in the API.
4. The only scenario where it works is with bulk publishing only, i.e., site generated via the `generateOutput` API.
5. Detailed steps are available in the screen-sharing session recording : [https://adobe-my.sharepoint.com/:v:/p/tnetake/ERrRpzvOfHNFqO1GerZo--kBFCYJK6ToWgynlZo8welIoQ?referrer=Teams.TEAMS-ELECTRON&referrerScenario=MeetingChicletGetLink.view.view]
6. Also, I have tried to reproduce it on AEM vanilla 6.5 SP 20 with Guides version 4.4.0.40  
h3. Customer Impact and Business Urgency

This issue is impacting the customer's ability to publish updated and localized content on their AEM sites, which is crucial for their business operations. Given the nature of the issue and its replication on a vanilla AEM instance, it is being treated with high urgency.
h3. Potentially Related JIRA Tickets

The following JIRA tickets have been identified as potentially related to the customer's issue, indicating a pattern of similar issues across different setups:
 * DXML-5421: Incremental publish does not update content if the topic is edited locally and reuploaded.
 * SITES-4419: "Publish later" publishes outdated content of a page.
 * SITES-5370: Preview URLs not generated anymore.
 * GRANITE-38871: Dispatcher invalidation not triggered after content publishing on the local Cloud SDK.
 * ASSETS-14217: New Asset version not reflected on Sites instance.
 * DXML-12600: AEM site Publishing not working when multiple topics selected from the map panel.
 * SITES-14542: MSM | Rollout action on a blueprint page is not republishing the live copy page.
 * DXML-14902: AEM site publishing completion not indicated for user-created AEM site preset type.
 * DXML-14215: Incremental Publishing should be available when at least the map is fully generated.
 * DXML-7605: MAP's topic tab not picking the latest version of the topics and causing incremental publishing failure.

h3. Next Steps and Recommendations

1. Review the customer's configuration for the incremental API call.
2. Investigate error logs for clues related to the site generation process.
3. Consult documentation and engineering for further guidance if the issue persists.
h3. Additional Information

The customer is not an AEM Managed Services customer. The program and environment details are as follows:

*Program ID:* ATLAS-6

*Environment ID:* QA Author environment

Full investigation available here: [https://aemcs-workspace.adobe.com/bot/dynamics/investigation/7431f7a1-468f-4f8e-a6d0-1f1f75e79216]
human_ac:
[~vinodgupta] : I discussed this with [~pradyumana] and we found that the issue is that here incremental publishing is not able to handle conref'd topic properly. And this is most likely a break due to handling of referenced content DXML-12099 - where all the indirect references were excluded to avoid page generation for them. 

So the issue is:
 * If a map has topics referred in it and one of those topics does conref to a paragraph of another topic(which is part of this map)
 * When publishing full map everything works fine - all topics are published and updated as well
 * When doing incremental publish (selecting all topics) - it will not update the topic that was conrefd in one of the topics of the map

Attaching a package with sample content ([^DXML-16666-samplecontent.zip]) - where you can see:
 * The main map "the big M" has references to "ac1", "ac2", "svg-test", "sub-map1", "ac3"
 * When you publish the complete map you will see pages generated for "ac1", "ac2", "svg-test", "ac3" _(note that "ac4" was referenced from "ac3" but its page is not needed as its a indirect reference - this is expected)_
 * Do incremental publish by - going to map dashboard > Topics tab > select all items of map _(which will be "ac1", "ac2", "svg-test", "sub-map1", "ac3")_ > and regenerate. You will note that only "ac1","svg-test", "ac3" will get updated - incremental publishing ignored "ac2" which was conref but still a valid direct reference

 

 

*Analysis*

As per analysis with Pradyuman - with incremental publishing the conrefTargets are calculated correctly but the hrefTargets are blank - as the logic builds hrefTargets from the main map reference - and in incremental publishing the main map is not processed

*Request*

This enhancement request is in continuation to use case that was reported in DXML-11978 where any AEM Site pages that are generated from the ditamap elements "topicgroup" or "topichead" in a non-english map where the pagename that form the URL are not in control of the user and are not SEO friendly because currently with all the available configuration the best we are able to do is:
 * avoid AEM Site pagenames as "-" for topichead/topicgroup references: where in case all the characters of navtitle are special (like in case of korean or japanese)  - which was handled by providing the configuration "{_}System driven pagenames having special characters{_}" which renames such pages same as child page names (DXML-11978)
 * and in case of topicrefs/mapref etc where the title can be wrong - are replaced by filename instead of title

However, the URL formed even with such changes are still not SEO friendly and consistent. And choosing filename over title is still considered a workaround as:
 * the filenames are internal names which may not be relevant to content
 * filenames are not SEO friendly

 

*Ask*

As we also discussed internally we need to handle the URL formation in better way by considering below facts:
 * The URL formation should ideally be title based, as this is the best way to represent the content and makes them SEO friendly
 * The grouping elements of map like "topicgroup"/"topichead" in  maps should be handled in a special way specifically for AEM Sites _{color:#505f79}as only with AEM Sites we create a node/page(that forms the URL) corresponding to these elements{color}_ - so that the URL remains valid and understandable

_Omitting the approach that Lexmark proposed (using data name on topicgroup/topichead for non-english content) as it required changes in content to change the URL._ As we discussed internally and I have also confirmed with Lexmark below is what we need:

 

Instead of creating pages for topichead/topicgroup which impacts the URL and page hierarchy we should consider following:
 * The output pages generated will not have nested structure for topicgroup/topichead i.e.
 * The page hierarchy will not create a page for topicgroup/topichead - hence the URL pattern management is not needed
 * The TOC will still show the hierarchical structure where the title of topicgroup/topichead will be as authored
 * Just like how it works in HTML5 output.
 * We will also disable the link corresponding to elements like "topichead"/"topicgroup" in TOC and breadcrumb 
 * You can refer *_[1]_* representing the above explanation
 

With this:
 * we do not need any changes in the content XML structure or in the configurations to control url pattern
 * the behaviour of generated output will be just like other DITA-OT outputs and nothing specific to AEM Sites will have to be handled then
 * node-sanitization logic will not be needed for topicgroup/topichead elements
 ** using filename instead of title - is not anyways applicable to topicgroup, but any workarounds we did to handle this scenario can be removed 
 ** change to lower case or replace special characters will also not be needed as with this approach we are not creating pages for topicgroup/topichead
 

*Things to consider* while developing/testing:
 * Node sanitization logic will not apply to the topicgroup/topichead with tihs approach
 * We should still *put this behind a configuration* so as to avoid any disruption for existing customers who may not want to move to new logic

summary: Marketing and Techdocs content to co-exist | need way to by-pass post processing of Guides
description:
*Use Case*

We promote and we support Marketing and Techdocs content to co-exist on same instance of AEM. Techdocs teams can upload, author, translate content using web-editor, but marketing team would continue to create, translate preview content using Assets and Sites UI.

Problem comes with UUID setup on cloud - where if a assets is uploaded via Assets UI - NUI service will run and process the asset including post processing of Guides which will assign a UUID to it.

Since this UUID should be unique in repository - so when marketing team translates this content using Assets UI - the translated content deletes the source content as they are translating that content using Assets UI - which does not assign a new GUID - that logic is only tied to webeditor's translation UI.

 

Note that the marketing and techdocs content is mutually exclusive and there is no cross reference between the two.

 

So to support such scenario - it is needed that we should allow two folders which are mutually exclusive - and post processing of AEM Guides can be bypassed on that folder. 

Also, consider that there should be a way to define such rule as regex, as marketing team can create multiple root folders on the fly - so pre-assigning permissions/ACLs would not work.

 

*ANALYSIS*

On non-cloud there was a way to use DAM Update Asset launcher configuration to run Guides post processing on specific folder only - by using the globbing expression. But on cloud the only way is to use the config {color:#0747a6}/var/dxml/postprocess/ignoredPaths{color} which currently is very limiting as one can only define one path at a time. We need following changes atleast if this is the solution:
 * support for regex in each entry
 * support to apply negation rule, so that if there are many root folders to ignore but only one techdocs folder at root, then it should have a way to run post processing on only one root folder
